entities.summary:
The Battle of Cambrai was a pivotal engagement fought on November 20, 1917, during the First World War. Taking place in the Cambrai region of northern France, this battle was a clash of tanks between British and German forces, marking one of the first large-scale uses of armored warfare.

The battle saw the introduction of over 400 British Mark IV tanks, which initially broke through the German lines, but ultimately failed to secure a decisive victory. The Germans were able to regroup and counterattack, forcing the British to retreat.

The Battle of Cambrai had significant consequences, as it marked a shift in the way modern warfare was fought. The use of tanks became a standard feature of Western Front battles, and the engagement paved the way for the development of mechanized warfare.

The legacy of the Battle of Cambrai can be seen in the continued evolution of tank warfare, with its innovations influencing the development of armored forces in the decades that followed. As one historian noted, 'The tank, born in the fire of Cambrai, would go on to shape the face of modern warfare.'
